findings.title: bucketTake writes down a borrower's debt using an impaired bucket deposit claim before other bad debt is recognized
findings.evidence: In TakerActions.bucketTake the target borrower's debt is reduced at line 168 (borrower.t0Debt = vars.t0BorrowerDebt - vars.t0RepayAmount). t0RepayAmount is produced by _calculateTakeFlowsAndBondChange (lines 749-774), which values the chosen bucket's quote deposit claim at face value via quoteTokenAmount = unscaledDeposit * bucketScale and divides it by the auction price, without requiring that this deposit already absorbed the bad debt of other undercollateralized loans. bucketTake only checks auctionPrice <= bucketPrice (line 439) and does not require the auction price to be at/below the external market price, so a high-priced bucket can be used. Reachable permissionlessly on any auction older than the 1h cooldown (line 699): an attacker can (1) deposit into a very high price bucket, (2) open a dust-collateralized loan A against it, (3) open a large well-collateralized loan B, (4) self-kick A then B so A's kick penalty pushes LUP to MIN_PRICE and B becomes liquidatable, and (5) after the cooldown call bucketTake(B, depositTake=false, highPriceIndex). The impaired bucket claim repays almost all of B's t0Debt at line 168 while only a small slice of B's collateral moves into the bucket; _rewardBucketTake (line 625) then mints the difference-value LP to the taker, who withdraws most of B's real collateral. The unpaid dust bad debt of A is left for the remaining bucket depositors/reserves, i.e. the workflow allows an already loss-bearing deposit claim to extract a healthy borrower's collateral before the loss is recognized and allocated (the on-chain Ajna protocol compromise).
